name: Rockwall
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Rockwall, TX 2026
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Rockwall, TX: Hometown Christmas and the Kiwanis parade, Breakfast with Santa, The Harbor tree lighting and Christmas on the Farm.
lede: The story of Christmas in Rockwall is one long Saturday downtown: the Kiwanis Christmas Parade, which the city counts as its 57th in 2026, followed by the Hometown Christmas Festival on the square and the 43rd annual tree lighting at City Hall. In 2026 The Harbor adds a first annual tree lighting of its own, planned with the city and the Rockwall Area Chamber of Commerce.
sections: Hometown Christmas, from parade to tree lighting

The City of Rockwall packs its biggest holiday day into one Saturday. The Kiwanis Christmas Parade starts it at 9 am, with more than 100 floats rolling about a mile and a half from the Rockwall County Library on Yellowjacket Lane to historic downtown. The Hometown Christmas Festival then fills the square from 10 am to 5 pm, with Santa and the Grinch in San Jacinto Plaza, a snow play area, bounce houses, crafts and train rides. At dusk families cross to the City Hall campus for the tree lighting, which the city numbers as its 43rd in 2026. In 2025 the parade theme was Christmas in Toyland, and the closing ceremony offered cookies, cocoa and crafts with Santa.
The wall that named the town

Rockwall takes its name from something hidden underground. The Rockwall County Historical Foundation records that in 1852 Benjamin Boydstun, Terry Utley Wade and William Clay Stevenson found a rock formation while digging a well, a buried wall of stone. KERA reported in 2025 that the formation runs about 20 miles and reaches up to seven stories tall in places, and that the City of Rockwall had bought the land where it was first found, hoping to let the public see it for the first time in decades. In 1909 Sidney Paige wrote about it in Science magazine under the title The Rock Wall of Rockwall, Texas.

Rockwall has no passenger rail station of its own, but the DART Blue Line ends next door in Rowlett. DART opened its 4.5 mile Blue Line extension from Downtown Garland Station to Downtown Rowlett Station on December 3, 2012, which makes Rowlett the closest light rail stop for Rockwall families heading into Dallas. Closer to home, train rides are part of the children's area at the Hometown Christmas Festival on the downtown square. For a bigger train day, the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano, the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco and the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley in Dallas all have Rally pages of their own.
